available_tools.name: create_project
available_tools.description: Creates a new Stitch project. A project is a container for UI designs and frontend code.

title.description: Optional. The title of the project.

available_tools.name: get_project
available_tools.description: Retrieves the details of a specific Stitch project using its project name.

name.description: Required. Identifier. The resource name of the project to retrieve. Format: `projects/{project}` Example: `projects/4044680601076201931`

available_tools.name: list_projects
available_tools.description: Lists all Stitch projects accessible to the user. By default, it lists projects owned by the user.

filter.description: Optional. A filter to apply to the list of projects, following a subset of AIP-160. This service supports filtering on the `view` field. name.description: Required. Identifier. The resource name of the screen to retrieve. Format: `projects/{project}/screens/{screen}` Example: `projects/4044680601076201931/screens/98b50e2ddc9943efb387052637738f61`

projectId.description: Required. The project ID of screen to retrieve. Example: `4044680601076201931`, without the `projects/` prefix.

screenId.description: Required. The screen ID of screen to retrieve. Example: `98b50e2ddc9943efb387052637738f61`, without the `screens/` prefix.

available_tools.name: generate_screen_from_text
available_tools.description:
Generates a new screen within a project from a text prompt.

**Instructions for Tool Call:**
*  This action can take a few minutes to complete. Please be patient. DO NOT RETRY.
*  If the tool call fails due to connection error, the generation process may still succeed. Please try to get the screen with `get_screen` method later.

**Output:**
*  **`output_components`**: If `output_components` contains text, return it to the user. If `output_components` contains suggestions (e.g. "Yes, make them all"), present these suggestions to the user. If the user accepts one of the suggestions, call `generate_screen_from_text` again with `prompt` set to the accepted suggestion.

available_tools.name: create_design_system
available_tools.description:
Creates a new design system for a project. Use this tool when the user wants to set or update the overall visual theme, style, or branding of the application.
This includes configuring:
- Color Palette: Presets, custom primary colors, and saturation levels.
- Typography: Font families (e.g., Inter, Roboto, etc.).
- Shape: Corner roundness for UI elements.
- Appearance: Light and dark mode background colors.
- Design MD: Free-form design instructions in markdown.
This tool establishes the foundational design tokens that apply across all screens in the project.

**Instructions for Tool Call:**
*  Call `update_design_system` tool immediately after this tool to apply the design system to the project, and display the design system in the UI.

DesignSystem.description: Represents a collection of guidelines, design tokens, and reusable components that define the visual and functional characteristics of a product's design. This is used to guide the generation of consistent and branded designs. LINT.IfChange

displayName.description: Required. Specifies the display name of the design system.

theme.description: Required. Specifies the theme of the design system.

DesignTheme.description: The theme of the design. Next ID: 15 LINT.IfChange

colorMode.description: Required. Specifies the mode of appearance of the design.

colorVariant.description: Optional. Specifies the variant of the dynamic color system.

customColor.description: Required. Specifies a custom theme primary color, or a seed color for the dynamic color system (hex format, e.g., "#ff0000").

designMd.description: Optional. Specifies a markdown file that describes the design system.

overrideNeutralColor.description: Optional. Overrides the neutral color for the dynamic color system (hex format, e.g., "#ffffff").

overridePrimaryColor.description: Optional. Overrides the primary color for the dynamic color system (hex format, e.g., "#ff0000").

overrideSecondaryColor.description: Optional. Overrides the secondary color for the dynamic color system (hex format, e.g., "#00ff00").

overrideTertiaryColor.description: Optional. Overrides the tertiary color for the dynamic color system (hex format, e.g., "#0000ff").

roundness.description: Required. Specifies the roundness of the design. Supported values are: "ROUND_FOUR", "ROUND_EIGHT", and "ROUND_TWELVE", and "ROUND_FULL".

spacing.description: Optional. Spacing units for the design system. Maps spacing names to their values.

typography.description: Optional. Typography scale for the design system. Maps level names (e.g. "display-lg", "body-md") to their Typography token.

Typography.description: A typography style token in a design system, defining the visual properties for a single text level (e.g. "display-lg", "body-md").

designSystem.description: Required. The design system to create.

projectId.description: Optional. The project ID to create design system for, example: '4044680601076201931', without the `projects/` prefix. If empty, creates a global asset (not associated with any project).

designTheme.designMd:
# Design System Document: Research Operations & XRML Intelligence

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
**The Creative North Star: "The Observational Monolith"**

In the world of high-density research and XRML (Extensible Research Markup Language) agents, noise is the enemy. This design system moves away from the "cluttered cockpit" trope of data dashboards and toward the feel of a premium, high-end editorial publication. We are building a "Monolith"—an interface that feels solid, authoritative, and impossibly precise. 

The system breaks the "standard dashboard" template by utilizing **intentional asymmetry** and **tonal depth**. Instead of boxing data into rigid rectangles, we allow information to breathe through expansive whitespace, using the "Monolith" structure to anchor the eye. We prioritize the relationship between a "label" and a "value," treating every data point as a piece of curated typography rather than just a number in a cell.

---

## 2. Colors: Tonal Atmosphere
We do not use color to decorate; we use it to signify state and depth. The palette is rooted in a "Deep Navy" foundation with "Vibrant Accents" that slice through the darkness like laser precision.

### The "No-Line" Rule
**Explicit Instruction:** Prohibit the use of 1px solid borders for sectioning. Boundaries must be defined solely through background color shifts or subtle tonal transitions. Use `surface-container-low` (#131b2e) against the `surface` (#0b1326) background to define areas. If the UI feels "lost," adjust the tonal step, do not draw a line.

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as a series of physical layers—like stacked sheets of obsidian.
*   **Base:** `surface` (#0b1326) – The canvas.
*   **Primary Containers:** `surface-container` (#171f33) – For main data blocks.
*   **Active Overlays:** `surface-container-high` (#222a3d) – For focused research nodes.

### The "Glass & Gradient" Rule
To elevate the "local-first" agent feel, use Glassmorphism for floating command palettes.
*   **Floating Elements:** Use `surface-container-highest` (#2d3449) at 70% opacity with a `24px` backdrop-blur.
*   **Signature Textures:** For primary actions, use a subtle linear gradient from `primary` (#c3c0ff) to `primary-container` (#4f46e5) at a 135-degree angle. This provides a "liquid metal" sheen that flat indigo cannot match.

---

## 3. Typography: Editorial Precision
We use **Inter** as our sole typeface, relying on extreme weight contrast and scale to drive the hierarchy.

*   **Data Values vs. Labels:** 
    *   Values use `title-md` (1.125rem) or `headline-sm` (1.5rem) in `on-surface` (#dae2fd) with Medium weight.
    *   Labels use `label-sm` (0.6875rem) in `on-surface-variant` (#c7c4d8) with Bold/Uppercase tracking (+0.05em).
*   **The Narrative Flow:** Use `display-sm` for aggregate research totals. The large scale creates a "hero" moment for the most critical data point, forcing the rest of the dashboard into a supporting role.

---

## 4. Elevation & Depth
In this system, elevation is a function of light, not lines.

*   **Tonal Layering:** Depth is achieved by "stacking." Place a `surface-container-lowest` card on a `surface-container-low` section to create a soft, natural inset effect.
*   **Ambient Shadows:** For floating modals or agent popovers, use an extra-diffused shadow: `0px 24px 48px rgba(6, 14, 32, 0.5)`. The shadow color is derived from `surface-container-lowest` to ensure it feels like a natural occlusion of light.
*   **The "Ghost Border" Fallback:** If a border is required for extreme high-density accessibility, use `outline-variant` (#464555) at **15% opacity**. It should be felt, not seen.

---

## 5. Components: Precision Primitives

### Buttons
*   **Primary (The Agent Action):** Indigo gradient (`primary` to `primary-container`). Roundedness: `md` (0.375rem). No shadow; use a 1px inner-glow (top-down) using `on-primary-fixed-variant`.
*   **Secondary (Status-Driven):** For "Active" states, use `secondary-container` (#00a572) with `on-secondary-container` text. This Emerald hue signifies the agent is "Live."

### High-Density Data Cards
*   **Forbid Dividers:** Never use a horizontal rule to separate list items. Use 16px of vertical whitespace or a subtle background hover state shift to `surface-bright` (#31394d).
*   **The "Node" Chip:** Use `secondary` (#4edea3) for "Active" status chips and `tertiary` (#ffb95f) for "Scheduled." Use a `0.125rem` (sm) corner radius to keep them feeling clinical and "pro."

### Input Fields
*   **Local-First Search:** A `surface-container-lowest` (#060e20) background with a `Ghost Border`. On focus, the border disappears and is replaced by a `primary` (#c3c0ff) 1px bottom-glow.

### Research-Specific Components
*   **XRML Code Blocks:** Use `surface-container-lowest` with a high-contrast `on-surface-variant` for syntax. No borders.
*   **Telemetry Sparklines:** Use `secondary` (Emerald) for positive trends and `error` (Red/Amber) for anomalies. Lines should be 1.5px thick with a subtle glow (drop-shadow of the same color, 4px blur, 20% opacity).

---

## 6. Do's and Don'ts

### Do
*   **Do** use `surface-container` tiers to group related research nodes.
*   **Do** use `label-sm` for units (e.g., "ms", "kb") and place them 4px to the right of the value in a lower opacity.
*   **Do** embrace "Empty Space." High density does not mean "edge-to-edge." Group data tightly, then leave large gaps between groups.

### Don't
*   **Don't** use pure black (#000000) or pure white (#FFFFFF). Use the `surface` and `on-surface` tokens to maintain the high-end "Deep Navy" atmosphere.
*   **Don't** use standard Material Design drop shadows. Use Tonal Layering.
*   **Don't** use icons without labels in primary navigation. A "pro" tool values clarity over minimalism.

### Accessibility Note
Ensure that all `on-surface-variant` text against `surface-container` backgrounds maintains a 4.5:1 contrast ratio. When using `tertiary` (Amber) for status, ensure the text on top is `on-tertiary` (#472a00) for maximum legibility.

design_dna.design_dna_text:
# Design DNA: XRML Research Dashboard

## 1. Overall IA
The information architecture is centered around the **"Observational Monolith"** philosophy. The dashboard is a single-pane instrument where the **Main Workbench** acts as the stage for research data, flanked by stable navigation (Left) and contextual observation (Right). Data flows from the Workbench (selection) into the Inspector (deep-dive).

## 2. Menu Placement Rationale
- **Primary SideNav**: Houses the core lifecycle of research (Dashboard -> Topics -> Runs -> Evidence -> Reports). Placing this on the left ensures immediate orientation for the user upon landing.
- **Top Command Bar**: Reserved for global, destructive, or "creation" actions (New Research) and search. This separates "doing" from "navigating."
- **Settings/Status Footer**: Positioned at the bottom of the sidebar to indicate stable, system-level configuration that is accessed less frequently.

## 3. Wide Desktop Grid
- **System**: 12-column fluid grid.
- **SideNavBar**: Fixed 280px.
- **RightInspector**: Fixed 320px.
- **Workbench**: Fluid, filling the remaining `100vw - 600px`.
- **Spacing**: 24px (L) standard gutters, 16px (M) internal padding for workbench cards.

## 4. 1920px Behavior
- **Layout**: Full 3-column expansion. 
- **Workbench**: Topic Portfolio cards displayed in a 4-column row. Recent Runs table shows all available data columns (ID, Profile, Start, End, Status, Nodes, Latency, Cost).
- **Inspector**: Fully expanded and pinned to the right edge.

## 5. 1440px Behavior
- **Layout**: 2-column core. 
- **Workbench**: Topic Portfolio cards shift to a 3-column row. Recent Runs table hides secondary columns (Latency/Cost) to maintain readability.
- **Inspector**: Collapses into a toggleable Drawer/Sheet that overlays the workbench when activated via an icon in the Top Bar.

## 6. Narrow Responsive Behavior
- **Layout**: Single-column vertical flow.
- **Sidebar**: Collapses into a hamburger-triggered drawer.
- **Workbench**: Cards are full-width list entries. Recent Runs table becomes a simplified "Vertical List" of runs with status chips.
- **Footer**: A compact system bar remains at the bottom to show provider health.

## 7. Action Hierarchy
1. **Primary Action**: `New Research` (Top Bar, floating monolith gradient).
2. **Global Navigation**: Left Sidebar links.
3. **Selection Actions**: `Compare Selected`, `Start Selected` (Workbench actions triggered via checkboxes).
4. **Contextual Actions**: `Export Data` (Inspector view).

## 8. Card/Table Density Guidance
- **Principle**: "Compact Clinical." 
- **Tables**: Row height 40px. No borders; use `surface-container-low` background on hover.
- **Cards**: Minimalistic frames. Vertical whitespace (16px) is used to group data points instead of horizontal lines.

## 9. Drawer/Modal Guidance
- **Profile Add/Edit**: Always modal-based (Drawer or Dialog). This flow is ephemeral and should not occupy permanent screen real estate.
- **Run Compare**: Full-screen modal overlay to prevent background visual noise from distracting from data comparison.

## 10. Accessibility Notes
- **Contrast**: Maintain a 4.5:1 ratio for `on-surface-variant` text.
- **Keys**: `New Research` flow is triggerable via keyboard shortcuts indicated in the tooltips.
- **Statuses**: Critical status readouts (e.g., `fallback_only`) must include an icon for visual distinction and an ARIA label for screen readers.
- **Focus**: Blue primary bottom-glow signifies intentional focus on inputs.
